In this experiment, you will investigate the forces supporting a metre rule.
Carry out the following instructions, referring to Fig. 1.1.
Do not attempt to change the position of either newton meter by adjusting the positions of the
loops of thread attached to them.

metre rule

parts.label: a
parts.text:
Move the 1.00 N load to a distance d = 25.0 cm from the 0.0 cm end of the rule.
Move one stand slightly, if necessary, so that the newton meters are as near to vertical as
possible.
Read, and record in Table 1.1, the value FP on newton meter P and the value FQ
on newton meter Q.
Repeat this procedure for d = 35.0 cm, d = 45.0 cm, d = 55.0 cm and d = 65.0 cm.

parts.label: b
parts.text:
Plot a graph of FP / N (y-axis) against d / cm (x-axis).
On the same axes, and using the same scales, plot a graph of FQ/ N (y-axis) against d / cm
(x-axis).
Draw two best-fit lines, one for each set of plots. Show clearly on your graph which line is for
FP and which line is for FQ.

mark_scheme.text:
graph:



intersection at d = 50.0 cm to ±1 small square

content.html: A student does the experiment with the same equipment as you. He reads values of FP which are the same as yours but his values of FQ are all higher than yours by 0.10 N. Suggest a reason for this difference. Assume that your values of FP and FQ in Table 1.1 are correct.
